item.title: LASWA, Interferry complete ferry safety inspection training
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Waterways Authority (LASWA), in partnership with global trade association Interferry, has concluded Module 6 of the Africa Ferry Safety Development and Mentoring Programme to strengthen safety standards across the waterways sector. The training equipped maritime professionals with technical skills to audit and inspect commercial passenger ferries as part of efforts to improve passenger safety and compliance with international maritime standards. The module, titled “Survey and Inspection”, combined self-paced theoretical lessons from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) and Lloyd’s Register with virtual mentorship and practical field exercises. As part of the programme, participants attended a virtual “Ask the Expert” session on October 21 with Interferry specialists, Joep Bollerman, Francesco Ruisi and Darren Johnston, to discuss international ferry safety standards. This was followed by live condition and safety compliance audits at operational passenger ferry terminals, supervised by Sandra (Okoli) Ubong of ABS and Engr. Frank Fayinto of Lloyd’s Register. During the field exercises, participants applied an eight-step survey methodology covering preparation, onboard assessment and reporting. They were trained to identify safety deficiencies relating to hull integrity, life-saving appliances, fire protection systems and machinery, while applying the 5W+1H principle to ensure evidence-based reporting. The participants also learnt to classify identified risks into immediate, medium-term and low-priority interventions to facilitate timely corrective action. The initiative is supported by the Lagos State Government and the Special Adviser to the Governor on Blue Economy, Mr Oluwadamilola Emmanuel, alongside Interferry Chief Executive Officer, Mike Corrigan, and Ferrysafe Executive Sponsor, Shari Corrigan. With the successful completion of Module 6, the programme is expected to progress to Module 7, titled “Watchkeeping”, scheduled for November 2026. The next phase will further equip participating maritime professionals with competencies in vessel operations, navigational safety and effective watchkeeping practices. LASWA reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening professional standards, improving passenger safety and developing a more efficient, resilient and sustainable water transportation system in Lagos State and across Africa through international collaboration. item.title: Mining: Zamfara task force moves to reclaim gold fields
item.description: The Zamfara State Government inaugurated a 13-man committee to curb illegal mining activities across the state. The Secretary to the Zamfara State Government, Abubakar Mohammad Nakwada, inaugurated the committee on Friday in Gusau, the state capital. This was contained in a statement signed by Mr Sulaiman Tudu, the Senior Special Assistant on Media, Office of the Secretary to the State Government, issued in Gusau on Saturday. The committee, headed by the State’s Commissioner for Environment, Abdulrahman Tumbido, has broad membership across security agencies, traditional institutions, and relevant federal and state government agencies. Inaugurating the committee, Mr Nakwada said the initiative was part of the state government’s efforts to assist the Federal Government in formalising the mining sector in the state. The SSG charged the committee to work closely with security agencies and relevant regulatory and local authorities to identify locations where illegal mining is taking place and profile the operators. The committee will also ensure that even licensed companies comply with relevant laws and regulations, take adequate measures to prevent environmental degradation, and safeguard the safety and rights of host communities. In his remarks, the Chairman of the Committee, Tumbido, said the committee will work with reliable information, respect for the law, fairness and regard for the rights and livelihoods of the people. He added that the committee will ensure that its efforts contribute to lasting security, environmental protection and sustainable development in the state. item.title: Emir Sanusi to Governor Lawal: I am impressed
item.description: The Emir of Kano, Khalifah Muhammadu Sanusi II, has expressed satisfaction with Governor Dauda Lawal’s performance in Zamfara State. The emir was the guest of honour at the commissioning of the rebuilt and equipped Zawiyya Mosque and Islamiyya School in Gusau on Friday. The Zawiyya is one of the oldest Islamic institutions in Zamfara, with a long history of producing scholars across various fields. In his Friday sermon at the rebuilt mosque, Professor Ibrahim Maqari emphasised peaceful coexistence among people and the importance of cleanliness, particularly in places of worship. At the commissioning ceremony, the Emir of Kano, Khalifah Muhammadu Sanusi II, said that only those familiar with the Zawiyya’s former structure could fully appreciate the scale and quality of Governor Lawal’s work. He also emphasised the importance of keeping the rebuilt mosque clean and well maintained. He said, “The mosque should be kept clean and in good condition. We must maintain cleanliness when we come here because the mosque is a symbol of Islam. “I am delighted with this work. May Almighty Allah reward His Excellency. “I can see the good work you are doing in Zamfara State in education, health, security, and infrastructure. “I am not surprised, as I have known your governor since his days in the banking industry. I know his capabilities, and I am impressed by his performance and happy to see him doing such wonderful work as governor.” The post Emir Sanusi to Governor Lawal: I am impressed appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Zamfara gov’t builds another mega school in Gummi
item.description: The Zamfara State Universal Basic Education Board (ZSUBEB) handed over the site for the construction of the Gummi Mega School to S.H.T. Standard Construction Company Limited for the commencement of work. The site handover exercise was personally led by the Executive Chairman, accompanied by his team of engineers. The Gummi Mega School project, valued at ₦1.086 billion, has a contract duration of 12 months. The award of this project to S.H.T. Standard Construction Company Limited marks another significant step in the board’s efforts to expand access to quality basic education infrastructure across Zamfara State. It is noteworthy that the Mega School initiative had earlier been awarded for construction in Gusau, the state capital. The latest award and site handover in Gummi, Zamfara West Senatorial District, demonstrate the administration’s determination to extend the development of educational infrastructure beyond the state capital to other parts of the state. The project is aimed at strengthening educational infrastructure, improving the learning environment and providing a safe and conducive atmosphere for effective teaching and learning in the benefiting community. The initiative further demonstrates the commitment of the Zamfara State Government, under the leadership of Governor Dauda Lawal, to transforming the basic education sector in line with the administration’s Rescue Mission Agenda and Six-Point Agenda. item.title: Lawal approves training of teachers to revamp education
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State has approved further training for an additional 250 teachers under the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology’s ongoing capacity-building programme. The Commissioner for Education, Science and Technology, AbdulMalik Abubakar Gajam, announced this during a meeting with members of the Committee on the School Enrolment Drive. He also said the governor had approved the renovation of four additional secondary schools, bringing the number of schools recently approved for renovation to six. A press statement signed by the Public Relations Officer of the ministry, Bashir Abashiya, indicated that the schools are: Government Girls Unity Secondary School, Kotorkoshi; Government Girls College, Talata Mafara; Government Technical College, Kaura Namoda; and Government Day Secondary School, Birnin Ruwa. The statement said Governor Lawal also approved infrastructure improvements at Government Secondary School, Tsafe, following the allocation of part of the school premises to the Federal University of Health Sciences, Tsafe. In the same vein, Governor Lawal approved the supply and distribution of approved curriculum materials to more schools across the state to support effective teaching and promote uniformity in curriculum delivery. item.title: Zamfara among top 10 best performing states in fiscal viability – BudgIT
item.description: Zamfara State was ranked among the top 10 states in the Fiscal Viability Index, a new report released by BudgIT has revealed. The new report titled, “State of States 2026: States ‘ Performance on Pillar B/ Fiscal Viability,” was released on Monday. This comes days after a renowned economist and former Governor of Nigeria’s Central Bank, Emir Muhammadu Sanusi, said he was impressed with the transformational feats recorded by Governor Dauda Lawal in the last three years in Zamfara State. The BudgIT report assesses the fiscal performance of 35 Nigerian states in 2025, the organisation said. “We call this ranking “Fiscal Viability”, but the real name is: Can your state survive without federal handouts?” the organisation said while releasing the report said. “States that rank higher on the Fiscal Viability pillar demonstrate a comparatively stronger capacity to manage their expenditure obligations within the limits of their available revenue,” BudgIT said in the new report. The report explained that “True fiscal sustainability means a state can fund its public salaries, overheads and debt obligations from its own pockets, while managing the demands on its total revenue.” BudgIT is a civic organisation that uses creative technology to simplify public information, stimulate a community of active citizens, and enable their right to demand accountability, institutional reforms, efficient service delivery, and an equitable society. The new report said Zamfara came in 10th on the Fiscal Viability Index, scoring 74.97 per cent, with Enugu (98.38%) and Bayelsa (88.83%) states clinching the first and second positions. The report said Zamfara remained the second-least-indebted state in the federation, with a debt per capita of N19,464. Zamfara is one of the only three states from the northern part of the country that made it to the top 10 positions of the Fiscal Viability Index. The two other states are Gombe (78.07%) and Niger (76.03%), ranking 7th and 9th positions respectively. The report also examined how states generated revenue, managed public expenditure, sustained their finances and prioritised spending across critical sectors. The organisation said the 2026 assessment adopted a revised methodology built around four pillars: revenue performance (40 per cent), fiscal viability (30 per cent), debt sustainability (15 per cent) and spending on selected critical sectors (15 per cent). It also examined states’ dependence on Federation Account allocations, expenditure patterns, capital investments, debt obligations and fiscal pressures across the federation. “This edition introduces a revised methodology that gives greater attention to the developmental impact of public spending, with an assessment of expenditure in agriculture, health, education, and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH),” the report said. item.title: Sit-at-home: Business activities yet to pick up — Traders
item.description: …An empty street on a sit-at-home day By Steve Oko & Chinedu Adonu Commercial activities are gradually returning to the South-East region after years of an illegal Monday sit-at-home order declared by non-state actors crippled business and social life. While commercial operations are picking up in some states, others continue to lag behind. For example, the Anambra State Government had to forcefully shut down markets in Onitsha and other areas to compel traders to reopen on Mondays, yet many businesses still remained closed. The exact reason for this hesitation remains unclear, as the threat of the sit-at-home order has significantly receded across the region, with the violent attacks and harassment of the past now seldom witnessed. However, findings indicate that many South-East residents have simply grown accustomed to this forced Monday routine after experiencing it for so long. Consequently, many individuals—particularly independent business owners—now voluntarily choose to rest on Mondays. Furthermore, several rural communities have permanently adopted Mondays for communal meetings, neighbourhood policing, road repairs, and other civic activities. Ultimately, what began as a forced restriction has largely transitioned into a voluntary day of rest, effectively extending the weekend by an extra day.In Aba, Abia State, following disruptions associated with the Monday sit-at-home, major markets in the commercial city are yet to fully recover their usual Monday patronage. Although Aba, the economic honey-pot of Abia State, is gradually emerging from the disruption associated with the sit-at-home era, investigations have revealed that the psychological and political sentiments that sustained Monday closures continue to influence trading patterns in some parts of the city. The immediate-past Chairman of Ekeoha Shopping Plaza, Aba, Prince Tochukwu Aguguo, in an interview with SEV, said that while many traders now open their shops on Mondays, a significant number of customers still stay away from the major markets. Aguguo attributed the situation partly to lingering resentment over the continued incarceration of the leader of the Indigenous People of Biafra, IPOB, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, saying some traders and customers were observing the Monday restriction voluntarily as personal expression of solidarity. According to him, the situation is no longer principally about coercion or enforcement by any group, but about what he described as a lingering “wound” in the hearts of some Igbo people over Kanu’s detention. “Aba is gradually recovering, even though customers are not yet coming, especially in the major markets where we deal largely in wholesale. “The issue of sit-at-home is not really about force by IPOB or anybody anymore. item.title: Kebbi APC reconciles aggrieved members ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kebbi State has declared that it is united and strong ahead of the 2027 general elections, following a reconciliation exercise aimed at addressing grievances among party members. The Secretary of the Contact and Reconciliation Committee set up by Governor Nasir Idris, Engineer Ahmed Umar Faruk, made this known on Tuesday in Birnin Kebbi while briefing journalists on the committee’s activities. Faruk said the committee had completed 10 days of engagements across the state’s 21 local government areas, during which it met with aggrieved party members and resolved several complaints. He said those engaged included former commissioners, former members of the state House of Assembly and National Assembly, as well as other party members who felt sidelined or had grievances arising from the concluded party primaries. According to him, the committee recorded significant progress by providing a platform for aggrieved members to express their concerns and ensuring that their complaints received attention. He said the exercise had helped restore unity within the party, adding that the APC leadership in the state was committed to carrying every member along in its activities. “We toured the 21 local government areas in Kebbi State and saw loyalty to the governor and the party from top to bottom,” he said. Faruk urged party leaders at the state, local government and ward levels to sustain regular engagement with members to prevent grievances from accumulating and threatening party unity. He, however, warned members against engaging in anti-party activities and clandestine meetings capable of creating divisions within the APC. He said the party would not tolerate actions capable of undermining its unity as it prepares for the 2027 general elections. item.title: Tinubu Won 2023 Election On His Own, Buhari Didn’t Fully Support Him – APC’s Hassan
item.description: A spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Alwan Hassan, has said President Bola Tinubu won the 2023 presidential election against all odds, insisting that former President Muhammadu Buhari did not fully support his candidacy. Hassan said Tinubu secured victory largely through his own political strength, arguing that Buhari did not actively stand behind the APC candidate during the build-up to the election. He made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , while discussing the president’s chances of securing re-election in 2027. During the interview, Hassan was asked whether Tinubu would benefit from the organic political structure and support base associated with his predecessor, particularly as the APC prepares for another presidential contest in the next two months. In response, the APC stalwart questioned whether Buhari had given Tinubu the full backing of his political structure in 2023. “Did he enjoy that in 2023? Did we enjoy Buhari’s support in 2023? Let the truth be told, we did not,” he said. ﻿ When asked whether he was suggesting that Tinubu won the 2023 election on his own, Hassan answered in the affirmative, maintaining that the former president did not fully support his successor’s ambition. “On his own. Buhari didn’t fully come out to support Tinubu,” he said. He further argued that Buhari did not actively campaign for Tinubu during the 2023 election, despite both politicians belonging to the same political party. “Buhari didn’t do well in 2023. He didn’t actually come out to stand for us and stand for Asiwaju in 2023. Asiwaju won that election against all odds,” Hassan said. item.title: [VIDEO] Wike’s ₦10m Pledge: INEC, Police Can Trigger Investigation, Says Okoye
item.description: A former National Commissioner of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Festus Okoye, says the commission, the police and other law enforcement agencies can initiate an investigation into the ₦10 million pledge by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to councillors ahead of the 2027 general elections. Okoye, a lawyer, said this on Tuesday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He said the absence of action by INEC would not prevent individuals or other relevant authorities from raising concerns or investigating the matter if an electoral offence was suspected. “If INEC is not taking this up, can anyone petition on this matter to say, I think Minister Wike is doing the wrong thing? Is it possible? Oh, definitely, yes,” he said. ﻿ The ex-commissioner added that the state could also initiate action if an offence had been committed, while law enforcement agencies could investigate where they believed there were grounds to suspect a violation. Mr Okoye said INEC could equally petition the relevant authorities to investigate the matter and prosecute anyone found culpable. Wike had pledged ₦10 million to each FCT councillor who successfully delivers their ward for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 elections. item.title: Obi counters Tinubu, defends Anambra erosion record
item.description: Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), has disputed President Bola Tinubu’s criticism of his record on erosion control in Anambra State, insisting that he helped develop the programme currently being used to tackle the environmental challenge. Tinubu had criticised Obi’s tenure as Anambra governor during an All Progressives Congress (APC) rally in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, over the weekend, alleging that the former governor “ran away from erosion” while highlighting environmental projects undertaken in Lagos. However, speaking on Tuesday during an interview on Rhythm FM Jos ahead of the NDC town hall meeting in Plateau State, Obi dismissed the allegation as untrue. The former Anambra governor said he worked with a former Minister of Environment to develop the erosion-control programme, which he said was subsequently adopted following his intervention with the late President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua. “On what the president said while campaigning in Akwa Ibom, it’s not true. I, working with the former minister of environment, developed what they’re using today to fight erosion,” Obi said. “I went to President Yar’Adua, made a suggestion to him. He called the minister and said he should go and develop it.” Obi governed Anambra State from 2006 to 2014, during which the state faced significant erosion challenges. At the Uyo rally, Tinubu had questioned Obi’s preparedness for the presidency, citing the erosion problem in Anambra as an example of what he described as shortcomings in his record as governor. Explaining his visit to Plateau State, Obi said it was part of his approach to engaging citizens and understanding their challenges before embarking on campaign rallies. He argued that political candidates should first listen to the concerns and experiences of the people before explaining how they intend to address them. The NDC candidate also identified insecurity in central Nigeria as a major challenge, stressing the need to ensure that residents could return to their communities, pursue their businesses and engage in farming without fear. He said his administration, if elected, would prioritise public services, particularly education and healthcare, as well as insurance coverage for vulnerable Nigerians. “Unless children go to school without fear, unless parents go to farms without fear, we don’t have a country,” he said. “You cannot stay in a developing country and a developing world if you have poor health accessibility and poor education accessibility. Education and health are the foundation for development. I will invest in them.” The post Obi counters Tinubu, defends Anambra erosion record appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Benue LP disowns alleged political coalition, declares support for Tinubu’s re-election
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Labour Party (LP) in Benue State has dismissed reports linking it to any purported strategic alliance or political partnership with other parties, declaring that it remains an independent political platform committed to the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and the victory of all its candidates in the state. The State Chairman of the party, Mr. William Ochonu, made the position known in a statement, insisting that the Labour Party in Benue was neither part of any coalition nor involved in any strategic partnership with another political party. Ochonu in statement noted that “Labour Party in Benue State is not in any form of strategic alliance with any political party. We are not in a coalition. We are not part of any strategic partnership. We are Labour Party, and we stand on our own. “We have seen a list circulating in the public space with the names of highly respectable individuals under a so-called strategic partnership to deliver Mr. President. While we respect every name on that list and hold those individuals in high esteem, the Benue State Labour Party and its candidates are not part of any such partnership or alliance. “We do not need to join any alliance to do what we are already doing. On its own, the Labour Party in Benue State is mobilising Benue voters to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, and all Labour Party candidates in the state. “We are working for the re-election of President Tinubu because we believe in his leadership and want his administration to continue consolidating the gains of its reforms. His policies on the economy, infrastructure, security, agriculture and national renewal are laying the foundation for a stronger Nigeria. That is our conviction, and that is the basis of our campaign. “All Labour Party candidates in Benue State are on the field mobilising support for Mr. President and for our candidates. From the governorship to the Senate, House of Representatives and State Assembly, our message remains the same, ‘Vote Labour Party from top to bottom, and vote President Tinubu for continuity. “We are not running a divided campaign. We are running a united and focused one. In line with this, the Labour Party in Benue State will soon unveil its Independent Campaign Council for the Re-election of President Tinubu.” According to him, “There will be a Labour Party structure, made up of Labour Party members, working for Labour Party objectives. It will coordinate our mobilisation across the 23 Local Government Areas, LGAs, of the state.” He noted that “the party is not against any of its candidates forming personal relationships or alliances at their own level. That is their right. But as a party, we will run our own independent campaign structure for Mr. President. “We will not fold our identity, our logo, our candidates or our mobilisation into any other party’s structure. item.title: NDC Alleges Plot To Disrupt Obi’s Benue Visit, Govt Denies Claim
item.description: The Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused the Benue State Government of plotting to disrupt the planned visit of its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to the state, an allegation the government has dismissed as false. Obi is scheduled to visit Benue State on Wednesday for a town hall meeting in Makurdi and a humanitarian visit to Yelewata, where he is expected to pay tribute to victims of the June 2025 massacre and commiserate with their families. Addressing journalists in Makurdi on Tuesday, the party’s governorship candidate in the state, Terhemba Shija, called on the state government and security agencies to guarantee the safety of Obi and his supporters. Shija alleged that the government had issued threats aimed at preventing the former Anambra State governor from visiting Yelewata, recalling an earlier attempt to stop him from visiting the community. He said the party had notified the state government and security agencies of the planned visit, adding that its arrangements were already in place. “This letter addressed to His Excellency, the Executive Governor of Benue, was received on the 10th of November, which is today. “While we discuss with the security agency, all they require is that we should send them an itinerary of our visit. I’m going to soon embark on the visit of all the local governments. All I have told the DG to do is to write the itinerary, the times that we’ll be here, and then they will follow,” he said, displaying a copy of the correspondence. ﻿ Shija maintained that the party did not require permission from the state government to conduct its political activities but had notified the authorities in the interest of a peaceful visit. He described Obi’s planned trip as both humanitarian and political, saying the presidential candidate would lay a wreath at the cenotaph erected in memory of the victims of the Yelewata massacre along the Lafia Road. The NDC governorship candidate said Obi would also meet relatives of the victims but would not visit any government facility or internally displaced persons’ camp. According to him, the town hall meeting would be held at the multipurpose hall of the Mission House in Makurdi, behind the Benue Links head office in Wurukum. Shija alleged that the state government was unhappy with Obi’s visit because of its potential political implications ahead of the 2027 general elections. He also accused the government of being behind an earlier attempt to disrupt the presidential candidate’s visit to Yelewata, claiming that suspected supporters of the slogan, “No Alia, No Benue”, had mobilised to prevent him from accessing the community. He, however, urged Obi’s supporters to remain vigilant and peaceful, insisting that the party would not be deterred by the alleged threats. “The visit of Mr Peter Obi is going to be conducted in a peaceful atmosphere. item.title: Tinubu wants gas resources to improve Nigerians’ lives – Ekpo
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Hon. Ekperikpe Ekpo, has said President Bola Tinubu wants Nigeria’s abundant gas resources to translate into better living conditions for Nigerians. Ekpo spoke on Tuesday in Kano during the commissioning of two Liquefied Compressed Natural Gas (LCNG) facilities developed by Rolling Energy with support from the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF). He said the projects demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to turning its gas policies into practical infrastructure that would improve access to domestic gas. “The President has been unequivocal that Nigeria’s abundant gas resources must translate into real improvements in the lives of our people,” he said. The minister said the facilities would expand gas supply in Kano and neighbouring areas, provide cleaner energy alternatives, support businesses and transportation, and create economic opportunities. He explained that the Tamburawa distribution hub has LNG storage, regasification and CNG distribution facilities, while the retail outlets would bring gas closer to consumers. Ekpo also stressed the importance of private sector investment in developing the gas industry. According to him, government must go beyond making policies to providing infrastructure that benefits Nigerians. “Government cannot stop at formulating good policies. We must catalyse the private capital and infrastructure required to translate those policies into benefits that Nigerians can see, use and feel,” he said. Also speaking, the Executive Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG), Barrister Ismaeel Ahmed, said the expansion of refuelling stations would make cheaper and cleaner transportation more accessible to Nigerians. Ahmed, who was represented by his Special Adviser on Technical Training and Capacity Building, Mr Omoh Imoukhede, said the growth of CNG infrastructure must go hand in hand with vehicle conversions. “The conversation about energy transition cannot remain about what Nigeria can do with its enormous gas resources. Nigerians must begin to see the infrastructure, use the infrastructure and experience the benefits in their lives every day,” he said. He described Kano as an important location for CNG expansion because of its large transport sector and commercial activities, adding that more refuelling stations would encourage drivers and transport operators to switch to gas. “Conversion without refuelling infrastructure will not deliver the transition we want. The two must grow together,” he said. Ahmed commended the MDGIF, Rolling Energy and the Kano State Government for supporting the development of the facilities. item.title: Makinde Presents ₦1.115tn 2027 Budget To Oyo Assembly
item.description: Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has presented a proposed budget of ₦1.115 trillion for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly for consideration and approval. Tagged the “Budget of Sustained Progress”, the proposal is valued at ₦1,115,341,378,359.90. Presenting the budget on Tuesday at the Assembly complex in Agodi, Ibadan, Makinde said it was designed to consolidate the gains of his administration and lay a foundation for sustainable development beyond its tenure. He described it as the final budget proposal of his administration, saying it would sustain the state’s development momentum and ensure continuity after the transition to a new government. “As we prepare to hand over the baton to the next administration, we bring before you the 2027 Budget of Sustained Progress. It is designed to consolidate our gains, sustain public services and carry our state’s development forward through the transition period and beyond,” he said. The governor said the proposal prioritised infrastructure, community development and the strengthening of public institutions, with significant allocations for capital projects in health, education and road infrastructure. He added that his administration was committed to leaving behind clear records, properly documented processes and institutions capable of sustaining efficient service delivery. Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Makinde said Oyo State’s Internally Generated Revenue increased by 288 per cent, from ₦26.59 billion in 2019 to ₦103.25 billion in 2025. He also noted that the state ranked third nationally in the 2025 Subnational Ease of Doing Business Assessment. The governor said targeted interventions and partnerships had helped return about 65,000 out-of-school children to classrooms, alongside investments in educational infrastructure, recruitment and service delivery. He, however, said the administration’s performance should be measured beyond revenue figures and rankings. “Figures alone cannot fully assess our administration. The real measure of success is the impact we have made on the lives of our people and the institutions we have built to serve them beyond May 29, 2027,” he said. Makinde also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to women’s inclusion in governance, pledging to sustain the 35 per cent affirmative action policy for women. On infrastructure and agriculture, he said the government had prioritised strategic road projects to connect economic corridors, improve market access and create opportunities for farmers, businesses and rural communities. He said the establishment of the Oyo State Agribusiness Development Agency had helped reposition agriculture as a viable business sector, while the Oyo State Agribusiness Transformation Centre had become a hub for agricultural investment. item.title: Sanwo-Olu appoints Akinyemi as acting MD LAWMA
item.description: .Reviews management structure By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu has finally appointed Olajuwon Akinyemi as the acting Managing Director of the Lagos State Waste Management Authority, LAWMA. By the appointment, Akinyemi succeeded former M.D, Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin who was forced to resign following intractable waste management challenges across the state. When contacted, the state Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, on Tuesday evening, confirmed the appointment. According to Wahab, the new MD, who was the former Executive Director of Operations, will also serve in the capacity of Executive Director, Finance. Also, in the coming days, new officers would be redeployed in the restructuring effort of the management staff. This comes following reports of forced resignation of former M.D, Dr. Muyiwa Gbadegesin over the seemingly intractable waste management challenges across the state. This laid to rest earlier reported appointment of , Dr. Hassan Sanuth, Director Sanitation Services – Office of Environment in the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources as acting MD. However, Sanuth was temporarily drafted to LAWMA to assist in waste management pending appointment of substantive managing director. On October 19, indications emerged that Governor Sanwo-Olu has directed Gbadegesin to resign amid persistent refuse accumulation across the state. It was gathered that the governor became increasingly dissatisfied with Gbadegesin’s handling of the waste management crisis and had asked him to step down. Earlier in September 2026, during an inspection of the Olusosun Dumpsite in Ojota, Sanwo-Olu handed a strong warning against further failure to stop the menace announcing plans to overhaul the agency for effective management, describing Gbadegesin’s inability as “sabotage” According to an inside source, “the governor’s displeasure stemmed from the slow pace of waste evacuation and the alleged failure of Gbadegesin to act promptly on directives aimed at addressing the crisis. “The governor was at the Olusosun Dumpsite in Ojota a month ago and was dissatisfied with the state of things. He gave instructions that immediate action be taken on the matter, as he has declared a state of emergency on waste management. “The governor was upset when he observed that the situation had not improved despite his clear directive. So, over the weekend, he asked him to resign, although he is begging and has reached out to some prominent Lagosians to beg on his behalf.” Also, residents across Lagos have repeatedly complained about worsening waste collection, with refuse accumulating along road medians, streets and major highways. The prevalent parts of the state, include: Ogba, Idimu, Ejigbo, Mushin, Egbeda, Surulere, Ajegunle, Ikorodu, Ojo, Obalende, Apapa and Mile 2, where residents have had to contend with heaps of stinking refuse along streets and drainage channels. item.title: Embrace HIV testing as routine healthcare-Lagos govt urges residents
item.description: . Extends free screening to staff, trade fair visitors By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has urged residents across the state to embrace HIV testing as part of routine healthcare rather than wait until they suspect an infection before seeking screening. Meanwhile, the state government has extended free HIV testing and counselling services to public servants and visitors to the ongoing 2026 International Trade Fair as part of efforts to promote early diagnosis and expand access to HIV prevention and treatment. The interventions, implemented by the Lagos State AIDS Control Agency (LSACA), are aimed at bringing HIV-related services closer to residents, encouraging routine testing and ensuring that individuals who require further care are linked to appropriate treatment facilities. At the Public Service Week health screening exercise, the Head of Service, Lagos State, Mr Bode Agoro, officially opened the free screening programme and urged public servants to prioritise their health by taking advantage of the opportunity. Agoro said access to preventive healthcare, including HIV screening, was essential to building a healthy, productive and efficient workforce. He encouraged workers to embrace regular health checks and utilise the confidential testing, professional counselling and information on HIV prevention, transmission and treatment provided through the exercise. In a related intervention, LSACA commenced free HIV testing and counselling services at the Lagos Pavilion, Tafawa Balewa Square (TBS), as part of activities at the 2026 International Trade Fair. The exercise, which began on Friday, November 6, is scheduled to run for 10 days, ending on Sunday, November 15. It provides visitors, exhibitors, traders and other participants with access to confidential HIV screening, counselling, preventive health information and guidance on accessing treatment and care where necessary. The Chief Executive Officer of LSACA, Dr Folakemi Animashaun, reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to ensuring that HIV prevention, testing and treatment services remain accessible, confidential and free from discrimination. Animashaun said knowing one’s HIV status was an important step towards preventing new infections and improving health outcomes, noting that early diagnosis enables individuals who test positive to commence treatment promptly and maintain healthy, productive lives. She urged public servants, Trade Fair participants and residents across the state to embrace HIV testing as part of routine healthcare rather than wait until they suspect an infection before seeking screening. The LSACA chief executive also emphasised the importance of collaboration with Ministries, Departments and Agencies, development partners, civil society organisations and other stakeholders in expanding access to HIV prevention, testing, treatment and care services. item.title: ‎States must contribute to pension protection fund to benefit from minimum pension — PenCom DG
item.description: ‎–It is big shame for some state retirees to be paid ₦5,000’ ‎‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎‎ABUJA — The Director-General of Nigeria’s National Pension Commission (PenCom), Ms. Omolola Bridget Oloworaran, said on Tuesday that states must contribute to the Pension Protection Fund before they can become eligible for the minimum pension. ‎‎She stated this at the official launch of the Minimum Pension Guarantee Scheme and the unveiling of PenCare, a pension industry-funded healthcare initiative designed to provide low-income retirees with access to essential medical services free of charge. ‎‎The event was held at the Old Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja. ‎She said about 170,000 retirees are expected to receive the minimum pension of ₦52,500, including those who were previously receiving less than that amount. ‎‎“Every eligible retiree who earns below ₦52,500 will be uplifted to ₦52,500. So, of course, as I said, there is no discrimination if you are within the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS). ‎‎“However, there is an eligibility criterion at the same level. We are making it a requirement that states must contribute to the Pension Protection Fund before they can be eligible for the minimum pension. ‎‎“So, we will work out that modality at the state level because we all know that the fund needs to be sustainable. If people are not contributing, we will run out of funds, and we cannot start a laudable initiative like this and then, years from now, somebody says it has stopped working because people are not contributing. ‎‎“So, we are working on modalities for the states to start contributing. But, as of now, it does not apply only to federal workers. Even private-sector workers are receiving these minimum pensions. ‎‎“As I said in my speech, 54 per cent of the total number of retirees who fall below the minimum pension work in the private sector, even though the private sector is not the majority employer. Essentially, 65 per cent or more of private-sector retirees are earning less than ₦52,500. ‎‎“So, when we tell them to contribute to the Pension Protection Fund, there is a reason for that. They form a large chunk of the money we need.” ‎‎On whether anything was being done to ensure that retirees from states also benefit from the minimum pension, as some of them still receive about ₦5,000 monthly, the PenCom DG said it was shameful to pay someone such an amount, although she doubted whether any state actually paid such a paltry sum. ‎‎“Frankly, that is a big shame. What we have done is that we have started working with the states to ensure that they pay retirement benefits to their retirees and also put a plan in place to review pensionable inflation. ‎‎“I mean, receiving ₦5,000 is unacceptable. I do hope it is not true. I will ask my team to confirm. ‎‎“But ultimately, what we are trying to do is get all the states into the scheme. item.title: Awujale stool: Adele-in-Council sues Abiodun, challenges reconstituted interregnum committee
item.description: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council has dragged the Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, and members of the reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council before the state High Court, Ijebu-Ode, challenging what it described as an unlawful attempt to displace the traditional administrative structure of Ijebuland. Other defendants sued alongside Gov Abiodun are the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs as well as members of the recently reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council including High Chief Rasheed Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu Ode, Chief Chris Okunowo, the Bobasuwa, Prof Jide Ajayi, the Jagun Aso, Chief Stephen Bakare, the Babalaje as well as Chief Alade Shote, the Otun Balogun The suit dated November 5, 2026 and marked HCJ/201/2026 according to a statement from the Media office of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council and supporting court documents made available to journalists on Tuesday seeks to establish the authority of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council to oversee the traditional and administrative affairs of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum following the transition of the late Awujale of Ijebuland, Oba Sikiru Kayode Adetona. The nine members of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council led by the Adele and Ogbeni Oja of Ijebuland, Olorogun Dr Sonny Kuku, are asking the court to declare that the Adele system is the only legitimate traditional administrative authority recognised by the native law, customs and ancestral practices of the Ijebu people during the period between the reigns of successive Awujales. They are also challenging the establishment and subsequent reconstitution of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council, describing the arrangement as alien to Ijebu customary law and inconsistent with the Ogun State Chiefs Law. In the substantive suit, the plaintiffs are seeking a declaration that neither the state governor nor the relevant government authorities possess the power to create or reconstitute an administrative council capable of displacing the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council during an interregnum. They are further asking the court to set aside the purported reconstitution of the AIAC and the appointments of the fifth to eighth defendants, describing the appointments as irregular, illegal, unconstitutional, null and void. The plaintiffs also want a perpetual injunction restraining the governor, the relevant ministries and other government officials from interfering with or bypassing the customary administrative functions of the Adele Oba Awujale-in-Council. Similarly, they are seeking an order restraining the reconstituted Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council from holding meetings, parading themselves or exercising traditional, civil or financial administrative authority over Ijebu-Ode under the disputed AIAC arrangement. item.title: Only Rainbow Coalition can guarantee Tinubu’s victory in Bayelsa – PDP
item.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The Peoples Democratic Party ,PDP, in Bayelsa State has claimed that the Rainbow Coalition is central to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election prospects in the state, pledging to mobilise 300,000 votes for the President in the 2027 general elections. The state PDP chairman and leader of the coalition, Chief George Alabh Turnah, made the declaration in a statement issued by his Senior Special Assistant on Media and Communication, Kevin Loveday-Egbo. Turnah said the coalition would take its campaign for Tinubu’s re-election to communities across the state, with a grassroots mobilisation strategy targeting undecided voters ahead of the 2027 elections. He described the National Rainbow Coalition as a platform for engaging voters, explaining that the group would use its community-level outreach to highlight what it considers the achievements of the Tinubu administration and canvass support for his second term. The PDP chairman said the coalition was committed to expanding its mobilisation network across the state, adding that its target was to secure 300,000 votes for the President. He also challenged the All Progressives Congress, APC, to mobilise an additional 500,000 votes, bringing the combined target of both parties to 800,000 votes. “The Rainbow Coalition has pledged 300,000 votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in Bayelsa State. We are tasking the APC to deliver 500,000 votes to bring the total number of votes for the APC to 800,000 out of the one million, one hundred and fifty thousand Permanent Voter Cards collected in the state,” Turnah said. He said the coalition would intensify its grassroots engagements across Bayelsa as preparations gather momentum for the 2027 general elections. item.title: Three feared killed as gunmen attack mining site in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – No fewer than three persons have reportedly been killed following an attack by gunmen on a mining site in Jol community, Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident occurred at about 6pm on Tuesday, when the assailants reportedly stormed the mining site and opened fire on people in the area. A resident of the community, Bulus Shen, who confirmed the incident, told newsmen that the gunmen arrived at the mining site in the evening and began shooting sporadically. Shen said the attack threw the community into panic, adding that three persons were reportedly killed in the incident. The spokesperson of the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM), Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the attack. Tengwong condemned the killing, describing the incident as disturbing and unacceptable. He called on security agencies to urgently investigate the attack, apprehend those responsible and strengthen security around rural communities to prevent further loss of lives. Efforts to get further details from security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Why an Instagram Following Tracker Can Reveal More Than a Profile’s Follower Count
item.description: A popular Instagram account can attract thousands of followers, but that number rarely tells the whole story. For businesses, content creators, and people researching social media trends, another question can be just as interesting: which accounts does that person choose to follow? Someone may publicly promote fashion, technology, or entertainment while following creators in entirely different fields. A business account may begin following emerging influencers long before announcing a collaboration. A public figure may gradually change the types of accounts appearing on their Following list. These observations can provide useful context, particularly when viewed over time. An Instagram following tracker helps organize changes to the accounts a public Instagram profile follows. Rather than relying on a single snapshot, tools such as Snoopreport record detected follows and unfollows across reporting periods. The results can support social media research, although they cannot explain why someone followed an account or reveal information that Instagram keeps private. Why Follower Counts Don’t Tell the Whole Story Follower numbers are among Instagram’s most visible statistics. They influence how people assess popularity, reach, and sometimes commercial value. Yet having a large audience doesn’t necessarily mean an account has a clearly defined set of interests or strong connections within a particular industry. The Following list offers a different perspective. Consider a technology commentator who starts following several artificial intelligence researchers, software companies, and digital policy organizations. Those additions may suggest topics worth investigating. Similarly, a lifestyle influencer who follows numerous local restaurants might be exploring a new content category. Neither example proves a professional plan or future collaboration. Following someone can reflect curiosity, personal connections, or temporary interest. Still, when researchers compare several observations across time, they may discover changes worth examining further. The Difference Between Following and Followers Before using an Instagram following tracker, it’s important to distinguish two commonly confused terms. Followers are people who subscribe to an account’s updates. Following refers to the accounts that the profile has chosen to follow. For example, a creator may have 40,000 followers while following only 600 accounts. A following tracker focuses on changes within those 600 connections, not on identifying people who recently followed the creator. Instagram allows users to inspect the Following list of an accessible public profile. However, the list doesn’t provide a dependable chronological history of when each connection was added. The order in which accounts appear should not be treated as a reliable record of recent follows. To understand changes, the list needs to be observed across different periods.
